cards.front: Most complete molar pregnancies are karyotype [___] (paternal/androgenetic); partial moles are usually 69,XXY; ~15-20% of complete moles progress to GTN.
cards.context:
A complete mole usually forms when sperm fertilises an empty ovum and its chromosomes duplicate; less often two sperm fertilise it. There is no fetal tissue.

A partial mole usually forms when two sperm fertilise a normal ovum, producing a triploid conception with abnormal fetal tissue. Malignant risk is lower than after a complete mole.

cards.front: Planned vaginal breech birth is contraindicated when the estimated fetal weight exceeds [___].
cards.context:
The same list treats growth restriction below the 10th centile as a contraindication, not only a large baby.

Cord presentation, a hyperextended neck, and antenatal fetal compromise are also exclusions.

A planned vaginal birth is considered only for a frank or complete breech, and induction is not recommended.

cards.front: ECV for breech is offered from [___] weeks (nulliparous) or 37 weeks (multiparous); overall success ~50%.
cards.context:
ECV is manual rotation of breech baby to cephalic by abdominal manipulation. Done at 36-37 weeks (earlier baby may turn back, later uterus too tight + fluid too low); 36w threshold for nulliparous, 37w for multiparous.

Success ~50% overall, ~70% with multiparity/posterior placenta/adequate liquor (DVP >3 cm)/non-engaged breech/operator experience.

After successful ECV, baby usually stays cephalic; failed ECV → planned CS at 39 weeks.

cards.front: In birth suite, a woman receiving magnesium sulfate develops absent patellar reflexes and shallow breathing at 8/min. The obstetric registrar stops the infusion and starts airway support. The specific intravenous antidote is [___].
cards.context:
Absent reflexes with respiratory depression indicate clinically significant magnesium toxicity rather than the brisk reflexes of cerebral irritability.

Calcium antagonises magnesium’s neuromuscular effects. Stopping the infusion and supporting ventilation remain essential while the antidote is prepared.

cards.front: Substance use in pregnancy requires a non-judgemental approach with [___] reduction; abrupt cessation of opioids or benzodiazepines is dangerous.
cards.context:
Abrupt opioid cessation in pregnancy precipitates withdrawal in mother and fetus, risking fetal distress and preterm labour. Abrupt benzo cessation risks maternal seizures.

Frame as non-judgemental harm reduction — women who feel judged stop attending antenatal care.

cards.front: A positive hepatitis B surface antigen in a pregnant woman indicates [___] infection.
cards.context:
HBsAg is a viral coat protein made by infected liver cells, so its presence means the woman has hepatitis B now, acute or chronic.

Every pregnant woman is offered HBsAg testing at the first antenatal visit, because her baby can be protected at birth.

cards.front: Mastitis treatment: continue breastfeeding from affected side + flucloxacillin for Staph aureus coverage; abscess if [___] mass develops.
cards.context:
Mastitis is bacterial breast infection, almost always Staph aureus seeded through cracked nipples or milk duct stasis.

Antibiotics: flucloxacillin 500 mg four times daily (QID) for 5-7 days (cephalexin/clindamycin if pen allergic); analgesia + warm compresses.

Distinguish from engorgement (bilateral, no fever) and cracked nipples alone (visible cracks, painful latch).

cards.front: In antepartum haemorrhage, NEVER perform digital vaginal exam until [___] is excluded by ultrasound; speculum is safe but VE risks catastrophic bleeding.
cards.context:
A finger through the cervical os of a placenta praevia can shear the placental edge directly → catastrophic haemorrhage within seconds.

Workup: maternal history + vitals → speculum to visualise cervix + bleeding source (safe — doesn't enter os) → transabdominal USS to localise placenta.

cards.front: A growth-restricted fetus has slowing abdominal growth but relatively preserved head growth. Doppler shows falling middle cerebral artery resistance despite increasing placental resistance. This compensatory circulatory pattern is [___].
cards.context:
Cerebral vasodilation redirects cardiac output towards vital organs during chronic hypoxaemia. Reduced abdominal growth reflects the same redistribution.

A reassuring head size does not mean placental function is normal. The term describes compensation, not protection from all injury.

cards.front: Initial drug treatment of PPH uses oxytocin as a uterotonic plus early [___] 1 g IV as an antifibrinolytic adjunct; avoid ergometrine in HTN and carboprost in asthma.
cards.context:
Treat PPH concurrently: start uterine massage and an appropriate uterotonic such as oxytocin, and give tranexamic acid 1 g IV as soon as possible and within 3 hours of birth.

Tranexamic acid is an antifibrinolytic adjunct, not a uterotonic; a second 1 g dose may be given after 30 minutes if bleeding persists under the protocol.

Escalate uterotonics per protocol. Avoid ergometrine in hypertension or pre-eclampsia and carboprost in asthma.

cards.front: The classic triad of ruptured ectopic pregnancy is [___], vaginal bleeding, and unilateral pelvic pain.
cards.context:
The classic triad occurs in only about half of ectopic pregnancies; presentations may include GI symptoms, shoulder-tip pain or syncope.

Risk rises after previous ectopic, tubal damage or surgery, IVF, or pregnancy with an IUD in situ. Assess with TVUS and serial βhCG; an empty uterus above the local threshold is concerning but not diagnostic.

Rupture with instability needs urgent surgery. Stable, eligible patients with low βhCG and no fetal cardiac activity may be considered for methotrexate.

cards.front: MgSO₄ for fetal neuroprotection is given when imminent birth is anticipated before 30 weeks: 4 g IV loading dose, then 1 g/h infusion until birth or 24 h. The number-needed-to-treat to prevent one case of cerebral palsy is approximately [___].
cards.context:
MgSO₄ given antenatally for imminent preterm birth <30 weeks reduces cerebral palsy in survivors by ~30% (Cochrane). Mechanism is uncertain — possibly preventing glutamate excitotoxicity in the immature brain.

Regimen: 4 g IV loading over 20-30 min, then 1 g/h infusion for ≥4 h before delivery — aim as close to 4 h before birth as possible.

NNT ≈63: treat ~63 mothers to prevent one case of cerebral palsy. A modest absolute benefit, but cheap and low-risk, so given routinely at this gestation.

cards.front: In hyperemesis gravidarum, give IV [___] before any dextrose to prevent Wernicke encephalopathy (triad: confusion, ataxia, ophthalmoplegia).
cards.context:
Wernicke encephalopathy from acute thiamine deficiency strikes thiamine-dependent metabolic steps in the brainstem + cerebellum.

Catastrophic interaction: glucose pushes pyruvate down a thiamine-requiring step that's already starved → accelerates the lesion, risks permanent Korsakoff amnesia.

Cost trivial; harm of skipping is irreversible memory loss — same rule in alcoholic patients.

cards.front: In placental abruption, visible bleeding may [___] reflect severity; concealed abruption can cause DIC and fetal death with minimal external loss.
cards.context:
In abruption, blood may dissect between the placenta and uterine wall WITHOUT escaping through the cervix — concealed haemorrhage.

The concealed component drives DIC: thromboplastin from the disrupted placenta enters maternal circulation, triggering consumption coagulopathy, and the trapped retroplacental clot extends the disruption further.

cards.front: Non-invasive prenatal testing (NIPT) is a screening test analysing cell-free fetal DNA from 10 weeks; positive results require invasive [___] confirmation.
cards.context:
NIPT analyses cell-free fetal DNA fragments shed by placental trophoblast into maternal blood. The 10-week floor is when fetal fraction is high enough to call reliably; earlier risks an uninterpretable 'no result'.

It is a SCREENING test, not diagnostic — the DNA is placental, not directly fetal, so a positive can be confined placental mosaicism, a vanishing twin, or maternal mosaicism.

That is why a positive must be confirmed by an invasive karyotype (CVS or amniocentesis) before any irreversible decision.
